# Quantitative HCI Liquid Glass

> Agent-first behaviours, visual components and design tools built on Vercel UI SDK. React rendering; @ui-sdk/core and @ui-sdk/react pinned to 0.1.0-beta.13. Custom work remains Unvalidated by a human UI/UX team.

This is a private React workspace package, not a published npm release. Use the checked-out workspace and locked dependencies. Preserve existing application state and the shared material.

## Start here

- [Engineering guide](agent-engineering.md): choose, compose, extend, operate and verify.
- [Package guide](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/packages/liquid-glass/README.md): provider, material and component recipes.
- [Package instructions](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/packages/liquid-glass/AGENTS.md): requirements for future package changes.
- [Compact component index](/agent-index.json): choose by purpose, kind and public export; follow its `contract` URL for one complete entry.
- [Agent contracts](/agent-contracts.json): public export inventory, inputs, state, discovery, actions, restrictions and evidence.
- [Contract schema](/agent-contracts.schema.json): the versioned machine-readable contract format.
- [Custom action inputs](/agent-action-inputs.json): exact JSON argument shapes and examples for both custom primitives. Validate the shape before dispatch; inspect live state for revisions, valid IDs and host acceptance.
- [Release identity](/agent-release.json): package version, source provenance, content fingerprints and all emitted agent documents. Compare the page's `quantive-agent-contract-set` meta value with `release.contractSet` before using cached contracts.

- [Component and recipe registry](/registry/components.json): all SDK families, custom components and compiled composition recipes. This documentation does not provide another action endpoint.

## Choose a component

- [Application layouts](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/docs/hci/standards/app-layout-system.md): responsive shell regions, controlled navigation and workspace switching; host integration and the review-task model.
- [Layout quality](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/docs/hci/standards/layout-quality.md): bounded geometry/shift inspection, logical popup policies, SDK diagnostics and seeded failure cases. [Visual regression](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/docs/hci/standards/visual-regression.md) covers reviewed local baselines and optional hosted Chromatic.
- [Patterns and Assistant](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/docs/hci/standards/library-patterns.md): established command, filter, selection, detail, empty-state and assistant compositions on genuine SDK controls.
- [Patterns API](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/packages/liquid-glass/src/patterns/README.md) and [Assistant API](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/packages/liquid-glass/src/assistant/README.md): exact props, callback and host-state contracts.
- [Interactions and Sections](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/docs/hci/standards/interaction-sections.md): scoped effects, real context menus, semantic sections and cancellable chapter selection.
- [Models and transactions](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/packages/liquid-glass/src/modeling/README.md): inspect, preview, revision-checked edits, controlled acceptance and history.
- [Agent tasks](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/packages/liquid-glass/src/agents/README.md): capabilities, timeline, tool review, context and artifacts; local component schema, not protocol transport.
- [Graphics](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/packages/liquid-glass/src/graphics/README.md): layers, transforms, exports and host-owned image requests.
- [Package guide: Standards, shared canvas and images](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/packages/liquid-glass/README.md): composition and appearance APIs.
- [Modeling architecture](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/docs/hci/standards/agent-first-modeling.md): shared document, UWE/C4 scope and evaluation.
- [Engineering standard](https://github.com/45ck/hci-review-skill/blob/main/docs/hci/standards/agent-engineering.md): required evidence and future additions.

## Installed upstream authority

Read node_modules/@ui-sdk/core/skills/ui-sdk/SKILL.md and node_modules/@ui-sdk/react/docs/llms.txt first. Open only the needed component, rendering, agent and testing pages. Use installed declaration files to resolve exact types. Import SDK controls directly from @ui-sdk/react/<component>; never @ui-sdk/core/internal/*.

For a local checkout, the registry and schema sit at packages/liquid-glass/agent-contracts.json and packages/liquid-glass/agent-contracts.schema.json. Their hosted copies are served at the root paths above. Resolve source/docs/evidence paths in registry entries from the repository root, not from the hosted URL.

Read only the contract needed: `npm run glass:contract -- --search viewport`, then `npm run glass:contract -- liquid-viewport`. Hosted consumers can fetch `/contracts/liquid-viewport.json`. The full registry is available for tooling; it need not be loaded into every agent conversation.

Preflight custom action arguments without operating a UI: `npm run glass:contract -- validate liquid-viewport panBy '[80,-40]'`. The canonical entry's `runtime.actionSchema` is relative to the package directory. Hosted index entries and contract envelopes expose a separate root-relative `actionSchema` URL so it resolves correctly from `/contracts/<id>.json`. Schema-valid inputs can still be refused by current state, revision checks, permissions or the controlled host. SDK aliases continue to use the installed upstream documentation and live action discovery.

The compact index and individual contract envelopes link their own schemas. Each index entry carries the SHA-256 digest and UTF-8 byte length of its complete contract file. The release metadata lists the other emitted document files and their fingerprints. These are consistency checks, not authenticity signatures, browser test results or human approval. A dirty build reports its base commit without claiming a clean source tree.

The runtime is createAgent from @ui-sdk/react/agent: snapshot, query, act and subscribe. Contracts describe intended use; only executed tests establish that the described behaviour works. See the engineering guide for observable postconditions and limitations.

For model edits, distinguish `requested`, `applied`, `rejected`, `unchanged` and `applied-error`. A resolved host Promise is not acceptance: accepted document props are authoritative, including equivalent serialized copies. Inspect `pendingRevision`, use `cancelPending` to abandon an unpublished proposal, and pass the callback's AbortSignal to asynchronous host work. A failure after an applied change does not roll that change back.

## Composition layers

1. Import genuine controls directly from @ui-sdk/react/<component>.
2. Mount the existing LiquidGlassProvider from @quantitative-hci/liquid-glass/webgpu and kit.css at the app boundary. Reuse the provider when the app already has one. Supply the decorative backdrop deliberately: glass does not capture arbitrary application content.
3. Add @quantitative-hci/liquid-glass/interactions with interactions.css around the intended region. Add @quantitative-hci/liquid-glass/sections with sections.css around meaningful page content.
4. Keep one createAgent bridge from @ui-sdk/react/agent, with the host application's authorization policy. Use the SDK's snapshot, query, act and subscribe; discover fresh refs and current choices before acting. Observe the rendered state after an action, including a cancelled change.

## Application layouts

Import LiquidAppShell, LiquidAppRail, LiquidAppWorkarea, LiquidAppHeader, LiquidAppContent, LiquidAppInspector, LiquidAppDock, LiquidAppNavigation and LiquidWorkspaceSwitcher from @quantitative-hci/liquid-glass/layouts; load layouts.css after kit.css. Compose them under the existing LiquidGlassProvider and single agent bridge. The contracts are /contracts/liquid-app-shell-regions.json and /contracts/liquid-app-navigation.json.

- The seven passive regions accept children, className and HTML attributes. LiquidAppContent renders main by default; use as="section" with an accessible label inside an existing main. The shell owns positioning, not routing or permissions. An inspector's data-open="true" controls compact CSS visibility; the host owns dismissal, focus and preventing input into covered content. Use LiquidDetailSheet for SDK drawer behaviour.
- LiquidAppNavigation takes items {id,label,icon?,count?,disabled?}, activeId and onNavigate(id,ButtonActionDetails), plus optional label/className. Each destination is an actual SDK Button. The callback receives source and can return its asynchronous work; observe the host's accepted activeId.
- LiquidWorkspaceSwitcher takes approved items {id,name,role?,shortLabel?}, value and onValueChange(id,MenuActionDetails), plus optional disabled/className. Items have stable Menu values. Return the callback's Promise for SDK pending/error behaviour; MenuActionDetails exposes event, not Button source or change cancellation. The host owns permission checks and the accepted workspace value. A role label is presentation only.

The gallery's ?collection=layouts review task keeps workspace data separate, resets task context on a switch, refuses Viewer review actions and supports undo. Its account edits and review decisions use fictional in-memory data. Authentication, server authorization, persistence, revocation and audit belong to the consuming application. The standalone compiled recipe is docs/hci/examples/liquid-glass/src/recipes/application-shell.tsx; reuse its inner composition when a provider already exists. Custom layouts remain Unvalidated.

## Layout quality

Import captureLayoutSnapshot, compareLayoutSnapshots, inspectPopupPlacement, summarizeLayoutShifts, observeLayoutShifts and LiquidLayoutDiagnostics from @quantitative-hci/liquid-glass/quality. Load quality.css after shared kit.css for the diagnostics composition. Read /contracts/layout-snapshot-capture.json, /contracts/layout-snapshot-comparison.json, /contracts/popup-placement-inspection.json, /contracts/layout-shift-summary.json, /contracts/layout-shift-observer.json or /contracts/liquid-layout-diagnostics.json as needed.

- captureLayoutSnapshot(root, {scopeId?,maxTargets?}) is a read-only host hook over explicit data-layout-probe targets. Default limit 128, maximum 512. It returns scope/viewport/scroll context, bounded geometry and capture status. Invalid, unsupported or truncated input cannot establish a complete baseline. Stable bounded IDs must not contain personal data.
- compareLayoutSnapshots(before, after, options?) is pure. Position/size tolerance each defaults to 1 CSS px; expectedChanges is target/property/reason-specific and nonOverlapping names explicit independent target pairs. Ordinary scroll is compensated; changed scopes, viewport/zoom or ambiguous contextual scroll require a new baseline unless the applicable context change is deliberately allowed. Inspect status, nullable passed, counts and findings.
- inspectPopupPlacement(input) is pure. Supply trigger/popup/viewport rectangles and settled SDK side/alignment with the declared logical policy. Gap/padding default 8 CSS px, tolerance 1 CSS px. Missing actual metadata is unsupported. SDK positioning owns RTL/collisions; inspection detects anchor drift, gap, overlap, overflow and disallowed flips without moving controls.
- summarizeLayoutShifts(entries, options?) is pure: maximum unexpected-shift session, less than 1-second gaps and 5-second duration, with recent-input values separate. Default 128 retained samples, maximum 512, at most 10,000 supplied entries. Malformed/incomplete/unsupported evidence keeps cls null; bounded retained detail does not erase aggregate scoring.
- observeLayoutShifts({root?,maxSamples?,maxDurationMs?,buffered?,onUpdate?}) is a read-only host hook returning supported, snapshot() and idempotent stop(). Duration defaults to 60 seconds, maximum 300 seconds; buffering defaults off. It drains pending records, disconnects on stop/time limit/document hiding/pagehide, and retains only bounded probe IDs and rectangles. Root limits attribution only: native scores remain document-wide for the observed window. No arbitrary text, DOM references or telemetry is collected. Stop on host cleanup too.
- LiquidLayoutDiagnostics requires target: () => Element | null; optional label, active=true, defaultOpen=false and children. Real SDK Collapsible/Button children capture 64 probes, compare, record at most 128 samples for 15 seconds, stop and copy the local selectable report. It stops on close/deactivation/unmount, reports clipboard failure and remains visibly Unvalidated. It has no independent root actions and never changes layout positions.

Keep leading workspace/state menus bottom-start, trailing notifications/account/review menus bottom-end and compact dock More top-end, with logical SDK alignment. The private ?collection=layouts&quality=1 fixture deliberately tests faulty placements; do not expose fault injection as production behavior. Native observed-window CLS, recent-input geometry, reviewed pixel comparison and human usability evidence are separate. Browser scenario layouts_quality_seeded_geometry_and_fault_detection uses seed 0x51A7; utility properties use seed 20261122 with 200 runs. Missing Chromatic credentials explicitly skip only the hosted stage, never required local comparison or runtime checks.

## Interactions

- LiquidCursor({ children, variant: "glass" | "precision" | "native", disabled? }) scopes decoration. Glass uses a precise pointer dot and damped accent; precision follows directly. data-cursor-label supplies a short hint; data-cursor-media identifies a media region; data-cursor="native" explicitly preserves native behavior. Text entry, editable regions, canvas, disabled/pending controls and open native popups retain their native pointer. Keyboard input hides the decoration. The cursor respects effective motion and forced colours and never intercepts events.
- LiquidClickFeedback({ children, effect: "ripple" | "spark" | "none" }) adds a finite, bounded response around real activations. It changes no application state. Do not infer completion of asynchronous work from a press effect; display the actual SDK pending/error state.
- LiquidMagnetic({ children, distance? }) is for an aria-hidden decorative icon inside a genuine control. The label and hit target stay fixed. Never put another control or essential text inside it.
- LiquidContextMenu({ label, triggerLabel?, children, actions, onAction }) composes MenuContextTrigger, MenuTrigger, MenuContent and MenuItem. Actions are { id, label, disabled?, destructive?, requiresConfirmation? }. Keep meaningful, unique IDs and labels. Preserve the visible trigger for discovery and touch; right-click is scoped to the region. Return asynchronous work from onAction so the SDK tracks pending/errors. Keep confirmation on the consequential item, not on opening or cancelling. Host callbacks still own authorization.

Examples: docs/hci/examples/liquid-glass/src/recipes/cursor-feedback.tsx and context-actions.tsx. These examples are included in the TypeScript build and offered through Copy example in the demo.

## Sections

- LiquidSection({ title, eyebrow?, introduction?, actions?, headingLevel?, children }) supplies semantic section and heading structure. Supply real task content and actual SDK actions.
- LiquidShowcaseSection adds media, mediaCaption and layout: "split" | "immersive". Media needs a truthful description/caption and an appropriate accessible alternative.
- LiquidChapterSection({ title, chapters, value?, defaultValue?, onValueChange?, navigationLabel?, followScroll? }) keeps all chapter text readable and the selected media visible. Chapters are { id, label, title, content, media, mediaCaption }. IDs and labels must be unique. The SDK segmented control uses the same controlled value as scroll-following. onValueChange receives { source, reason: "selection" | "scroll", cancel }. Keep cancelled changes from updating the application state. Set followScroll=false for applications that own navigation elsewhere.
- LiquidSectionContour({ variant: "wave" | "ridge" | "orbit", edge? }) is decorative SVG, hidden from assistive technology. It is not a diagram or an information-bearing connection.
- LiquidReveal({ children, once? }) progressively adds a finite opacity response. Content remains present without JavaScript animation or when motion is reduced.

Examples: docs/hci/examples/liquid-glass/src/recipes/showcase-section.tsx and chapter-story.tsx. All four examples include a standalone provider; compose the inner content into an existing provider when integrating with an established app. They intentionally do not initialize another agent bridge: reuse the host's single bridge described above, or initialize it once at the application boundary.

## Patterns

Import LiquidCommandPalette, LiquidFilterBar, LiquidSelectionBar, LiquidDetailSheet and LiquidEmptyState from @quantitative-hci/liquid-glass/patterns; load patterns.css after kit.css. These follow familiar shadcn/ui arrangements using actual SDK parts. Read the package's patterns/README.md and one /contracts/liquid-<component>.json entry for exact inputs and evidence.

- LiquidCommandPalette uses SDK Dialog and Command with named grouped commands, search, shortcuts and pending/error feedback. Supply stable command IDs and onAction; return a Promise for asynchronous work. shortcut defaults to mod+k; pass null while a retained page is inactive to remove its global SDK trigger binding. Hidden ancestry alone does not disable that shortcut. The installed CommandActionDetails contains event only, not source/cancel. Cancellable opening and query changes retain their SDK details. Inspect the actual host effect after running a command.
- LiquidFilterBar forwards the SDK Input and multiple Select callbacks. The host owns query, facet values and derived results. Call details.cancel synchronously to refuse a value. Reset is a genuine Button action.
- LiquidSelectionBar displays selectedCount and actual Toolbar/Button actions. The host owns selected IDs and validates each bulk operation. It is not a selection store. Return callback promises and keep confirmation marks on consequential actions.
- LiquidDetailSheet composes the SDK Drawer with title, trigger, content, footer and close actions. It supports the real controlled open callback/controller and retains dismissal/focus behavior. The chosen record must be available when an agent opens the drawer directly.
- LiquidEmptyState is passive title/description/media/actions presentation. Put genuine SDK controls in the action slot; the wrapper has no root action.

The compiled work-patterns.tsx recipe demonstrates the package. The Patterns collection is local saved work, with real query/selection/record changes and explicit refusal paths. It does not include a table engine, backend or account system.

## Assistant

Import LiquidPromptComposer, LiquidAttachmentList, LiquidSuggestionList, LiquidMessage and LiquidSourceList from @quantitative-hci/liquid-glass/assistant; load assistant.css after kit.css. Their arrangements follow Vercel AI Elements and the cited 21st.dev prompt inputs, while all interactive controls use the pinned SDK. Read assistant/README.md for complete typed props.

- LiquidPromptComposer requires label, controlled value/onValueChange and onSubmit({text,mode},details). It offers an optional SDK input controller, modes/mode/onModeChange, host status ready|running, onStop, error, attachments/tools/hint slots and labels. The SDK Textarea supports Mod+Enter through the same submit path. Blank, oversized, disabled or invalid-mode submissions are refused; host props remain authoritative. No provider or upload is called by the component.
- LiquidAttachmentList takes attachments with stable id,name,description and optional disabled state. Its actual SDK remove Button calls onRemove(id,details); the accepted list comes from host props. Project context and local file selection must be labelled accurately. Compose the existing SDK FileInput when browser file selection is needed.
- LiquidSuggestionList takes stable {id,label,prompt,disabled?} records and onChoose(suggestion,details). The host decides whether this fills a draft or starts work; the gallery fills the real controlled draft.
- LiquidMessage is passive {id,author,role:user|assistant,children,meta?,actions?} presentation. It adds no markdown parser, streaming transport or root agent action.
- LiquidSourceList takes {id,title,url,description?} references and optional label/open/defaultOpen/onOpenChange. Its disclosure is the actual SDK Collapsible. Safe HTTP(S) links use SDK Buttons rendered as semantic anchors, so the bridge can discover them; invalid links become readable unavailable text. Source records are supplied by the host, not retrieved by this component.

The compiled assistant-composer.tsx recipe shows these composition boundaries. The gallery runs a clearly labelled, bounded local response fixture with cancellation, not an AI backend. Reuse existing AgentToolRequest and AgentTaskPanel when a conversation needs tool review or task history. Use one existing provider and one createAgent bridge; there is no second mutation endpoint.

## Chat and integrations

Import LiquidChat, LiquidConversationList and LiquidPromptTemplatePicker from @quantitative-hci/liquid-glass/chat and load chat.css after kit.css. The chat is controlled: messages, status, draft, accepted thread selection and execution belong to the host. Reuse the existing provider and one SDK bridge. The component's genuine SDK children expose human and agent controls without a second conversation store.

Use /chat/ai-sdk (projectVercelMessages), /chat/ag-ui (projectAgUiMessages), /chat/openai (projectOpenAIResponse) or /chat/anthropic (projectAnthropicMessage) for the matching optional SDK type projection. Each returns display records without operating the runtime. Unknown parts remain visible; hidden reasoning is not rendered. Attachment metadata is not an upload, and a tool disclosure is not execution or approval. Use renderPart with the existing AgentToolRequest for authorized review.

The Chat workspace demonstrates threads, templates, bounded local streaming, Stop and error/retry. The AI integrations page exposes actual compiled Vercel AI SDK, CopilotKit headless, AG-UI, custom-host and direct provider examples. OpenAI, Anthropic and OpenRouter provider configuration belongs on the server. These examples are typechecked against pinned packages, not live-provider validation. See packages/liquid-glass/src/chat/README.md and docs/hci/standards/chat-integrations.md for exact boundaries and source links.

The All components page exposes every canonical SDK/custom entry. Examples run the exact registered compiled TSX in separate documents; each standalone example has its own provider and bridge. Compose its inner content into the application's existing provider during integration. Sidebar search filters without changing the accepted selected page.

## State, preferences and review

Use meaningful accessible names and real UI SDK callbacks. Do not synthesize clicks to operate an agent-facing state model or expose a second mutation API. Decorative cursor/click/contour/reveal elements have no agent actions. Keep disabled controls disabled for all input routes. Respect data-agent-secret, data-agent-hidden and data-agent-confirm; the demo refuses actions requiring a person.

Honor reduced motion, forced colours, touch input and the selected material. Avoid endless animation, wheel interception, shifting hit targets and cursor replacement over native controls. Suspend effects when the document or collection is hidden and remove observers/listeners during cleanup.

All custom components remain Unvalidated until a recorded human UI/UX team review changes their status. SDK foundation identifies upstream behavior provenance only. Typechecking and browser checks do not establish improved human usability or WCAG conformance.

## Verification

Run npm run glass:verify and the repository's Python browser contract against the production build. Preserve all baseline scenarios, including interactions_pointer_keyboard_agent_and_preferences and sections_chapters_navigation_and_preferences, and include patterns_commands_filters_selection_and_details plus assistant_composition_cancellation_and_sources. Use the existing CI environment for software-WebGPU evidence. Record exact commands, source commit, browser, viewport, failed paths and limitations.

## Sources and reuse

The new React compositions adapt interaction vocabulary from CK.com and Wayrest: scoped cursor modes, fixed hit targets, decorative contours and natural scroll progress. References include https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/menu, https://magicui.design/docs/components/pointer and https://21st.dev/@automate_flows/components/liquid-glass-wordmark-footer. See docs/hci/standards/interaction-sections.md for precise provenance and scope. No premium Motion Cursor or redistribution-restricted React Bits source is included.
